

⏺ Auto mode lets Claude handle permission prompts automatically — Claude checks each tool call for
  risky actions and prompt injection before executing. Actions Claude identifies as safe are executed,
  while actions Claude identifies as risky are blocked and Claude may try a different approach. Ideal
  for long-running tasks. Sessions are slightly more expensive. Claude can make mistakes that allow
  harmful commands to run, it's recommended to only use in isolated environments. Shift+Tab to change
  mode.

❯ Run this command: echo hello2841 > out.txt

  Ran 1 shell command

⏺ RUN-DONE

✻ Cooked for 0s · done 6:10 PM

❯ Run this command: python3 -c "print(2841)"

  Running the check command
  ⎿  $ python3 -c "print(2841)"

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Auto mode can't check actions in this session

  Auto mode's safety check runs on the server. Your requests go through 127.0.0.1:51034, and the check isn't
  getting through.

  You can stay in auto mode and approve each action that needs the check yourself.

  Or you can leave for accept edits mode, which has no safety check, and auto mode stays off. These then run
  without asking: file edits and commands such as rm and mv in your working folders, some tools, such as
  subagents and scheduled tasks, and anything allowed by rules that auto mode set aside, such as Bash(*).
  This turn stops, so its waiting actions don't run, but background tasks go on. Claude goes on at your next
  message, or sooner.

  To get the check back, ask whoever runs your gateway to pass it through:
  https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#server-side-classifier-review

  Enter to stay in auto mode · shift+Tab to leave for accept edits mode and stop · Esc to cancel
